meta.route: London → Tokyo → Hakone → Kyoto → Osaka (KIX) → London (open-jaw)
meta.self_check: self-checked: 9 issues found and fixed — (1) Shinjuku Gyoen closes Mondays, moved off the 23rd onto Sunday; (2) Tsukiji closes Sundays, moved off the 22nd and its holiday risk flagged with a swap; (3) day 4 mixed an intercity move with 3 anchors, Hakone Shrine demoted to [skippable]; (4) day 5 likewise, the Sannenzaka lanes demoted from anchor to stroll; (5) day 7 held 4 anchors, Nanzen-ji re-cast as the day's optional extra and the Philosopher's Path tagged [skippable]; (6) walking totals rewritten from route_tools check output (day 7 is 7.8 km, at the 8 km ceiling); (7) the Gōra Station geocode came back ~600 m north of the station, hand-corrected; (8) meta.dates carried prose and broke the themed covers' date eyebrow, reduced to a bare span; (9) country-brief keys renamed to readable English headings because two of the three themes print the raw key. Verified-clean, not changed: every last-entry time against its planned arrival, all three rain alternatives against their own closure days, the 3 h airport buffer, open-jaw consistency across flights/hotels/day order.
meta.headless_note: Planned headless — no route-skeleton checkpoint was offered. The skeleton below (3 Tokyo / 1 Hakone / 3 Kyoto, open-jaw out of Kansai) was chosen for you; see decisions[].
meta.window: 8 days on the ground; the LHR departure is 2026-11-20 and the London arrival 2026-11-29 (see legs[]).

decisions: Open-jaw: fly into Haneda, home out of Kansai. It refunds the 2 h 15 Shinkansen backtrack to Tokyo and one more Tokyo hotel night. Cost: there is no nonstop KIX→LHR, so the way home has one connection. If you would rather have the nonstop home, swap day 8 for Kyoto→Tokyo by Shinkansen and a night near Haneda.

Dates 21–28 Nov chosen against the foliage ramp, not the calendar: Tokyo first (colour still arriving), Kyoto last (Kyoto's 2026 koyo forecast is ~25 Nov – 7 Dec). Going the other way round would have shown you two half-turned cities.

Three bases in eight days: Tokyo ×3 nights, Hakone ×1, Kyoto ×3. Hakone breaks the ≥2-nights rule on purpose — in Hakone the ryokan (onsen + kaiseki + futon) IS the anchor, and a second night would cost a Kyoto night in peak week.
No JR Pass. This route earns ~¥16,000 pp of JR travel; the 7-day national pass is ~¥50,000. Point-to-point tickets plus the Hakone Freepass win by a wide margin.

The two large cases are forwarded Tokyo hotel → Kyoto hotel by takkyūbin on day 4 (~¥2,300 each, next-day). Hakone is done on an overnight bag: the Tozan switchback train, the cable car and the ropeway are all bad places to hold a 23 kg case.

Monday 23 Nov is a national holiday (Labour Thanksgiving). That day is deliberately a market + garden + temple day inside Tokyo with an 07:30 start, not a Kamakura or Nikkō day trip — domestic crowds hit day-trip towns hardest.

Named restaurants are not in this plan on purpose; food is given as areas (Nakamise, Omoide Yokochō, Tsukiji, Nishiki, Pontochō). Kyoto restaurant listings churn faster than a plan written three months out can survive.

days.label: Into the volcano · lake · onsen

walking_km.how: route on foot 1.8 + Ōwakudani boardwalk ~0.5 + Gōra ~0.5 + the shrine's cedar avenue ~1.5

days.ribbon: Romancecar 85′→ Hakone-Yumoto →Tozan 40′→ Gōra lunch →cable+ropeway 35′→ Ōwakudani →ropeway 25′→ Tōgendai →cruise 30′→ Moto-Hakone →walk 14′→ Hakone Shrine →bus 40′→ ryokan

days.late_cut: miss the ~15:00 cruise → take the H-line bus straight from Tōgendai to Hakone-Yumoto and go to the onsen an hour early. Nothing here is worth arriving at the ryokan after dark for.

days.rain_alt: Wet stone on the Sannenzaka steps is genuinely dangerous in smooth soles. In rain, take the bus to Kiyomizu-michi and go straight up, then spend the gap in the covered Nishiki arcade instead of the lanes.
days.late_cut: the Shinkansen decides this day. Arriving after 14:00 → drop the Sannenzaka lanes and go straight to the 17:30 night opening; Kiyomizu's last entry is 21:00 and there is a lot of slack after dinner.

timeline.note: ⚠️ only a few Hikari services call at Odawara; if none fits, Kodama is direct and ~35 min slower. Fuji is on the RIGHT leaving Odawara — seat E.

Collect the forwarded cases at the desk · lunch near Karasuma — food area
City bus 207 · Hotel · Shijō-Karasuma → Sannenzaka · ~25 min · ¥230 pp
timeline.note: Kyoto city buses are flat-fare, pay on exit, and jammed in koyo week — the Keihan train to Kiyomizu-Gojō plus a 15-min walk is often faster

timeline.what: Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka — preserved machiya lanes, yatsuhashi and warabimochi stalls

Kiyomizu-dera · autumn night illumination

No reservation, normal admission. A single blue beam is fired over the city and the 1633 stage floats above a bowl of lit maples.

days.label: Bamboo at dawn · Nishiki at dusk

walking_km.how: route on foot 3.1 + bamboo path ~1.0 + Tenryū-ji garden ~1.2 + Nishiki arcade ~1.0 + Katsura riverbank ~1.3

days.ribbon: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove 07:20 →walk 5′→ Tenryū-ji →walk 11′→ Togetsukyō →lunch→ rail 40′→ Nishiki Market →walk 10′→ Pontochō dinner
days.rain_alt: Tenryū-ji's Hōjō veranda faces the pond under a roof and the Nishiki arcade is fully covered — this day survives rain better than any other. If the riverbank is a write-off, take the Randen tram to Ryōan-ji and watch the rock garden from the viewing hall.
days.late_cut: the whole day hangs on the 07:20 grove. Miss it and the grove becomes unusable until dusk — in that case reverse the day: Nishiki first, Arashiyama at 15:00 for the light instead of the quiet.

timeline.what: JR Sagano line · Hotel · Shijō-Karasuma → Arashiyama Bamboo Grove · ~35 min · ¥240 pp
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
timeline.note: no gate, no fee, open always. The 400 m path is empty before 08:00 and solid between 11:00 and 15:00 — this hour is the single biggest quality-of-trip decision in the Kyoto half.

timeline.what: Walk · Arashiyama Bamboo Grove → Tenryū-ji · 0.3 km · 5 min
Tenryū-ji
timeline.note: in the 15–30 Nov autumn window the garden opens at 07:30 (regular hours 08:30–17:00, last entry 16:50). The Sōgen-chi pond garden is 700 years old and unaltered — Musō Soseki designed it, and the borrowed mountain behind it is the koyo.

timeline.what: Walk · Tenryū-ji → Togetsukyō Bridge · 0.7 km · 11 min

timeline.what: Lunch · Arashiyama main street — food area (yudofu, soba)

days.label: Torii at dawn · maple valley · lit garden

walking_km.how: route on foot 1.8 + Inari climb to Yotsutsuji and back ~2.5 + Tōfuku-ji ravine ~1.0 + Philosopher's Path there-and-back ~2.0 + Eikan-dō ~0.5 — the longest day, right at the 8 km ceiling

days.ribbon: Fushimi Inari 06:55 →rail 12′→ Tōfuku-ji →rail 35′→ Nanzen-ji lunch →walk 15′→ Philosopher's Path →walk 13′→ Eikan-dō night illumination
days.rain_alt: Tōfuku-ji's covered corridors and Nanzen-ji's Hōjō rooms both work wet. Rain kills only the Philosopher's Path; replace it with the Kyoto Municipal Museum of Art in Okazaki, five minutes from Eikan-dō.
days.late_cut: drop the Philosopher's Path first, then Nanzen-ji's Sanmon climb. Eikan-dō's 20:00 last entry is the hard stop, and the queue there is the risk — be in it by 18:00.

timeline.what: JR Nara line · Hotel · Shijō-Karasuma → Fushimi Inari Taisha · ~30 min · ¥150 pp
Fushimi Inari Taisha
timeline.note: open 24 h, no gate. Before 08:00 the Senbon-torii is yours; by 09:00 it is a shuffling column. Yotsutsuji viewpoint is 30–40 min up and is the honest turn-back point — the full summit loop is 2–3 h and would eat Tōfuku-ji.

timeline.what: JR Nara line · Fushimi Inari Taisha → Tōfuku-ji · ~12 min · ¥150 pp
Tōfuku-ji
timeline.note: 8:30–16:30 from mid-Nov to early Dec. 2,000 maples in one ravine; the Tsūtenkyō bridge queues 30–60 min at peak and photography ON the bridge is banned during the peak window — buy the advance ticket, arrive at opening, shoot from Gaunkyō instead.

timeline.what: Keihan + subway · Tōfuku-ji → Nanzen-ji · ~35 min · ¥280 pp
Lunch · the yudofu row outside the Sanmon — food area
Nanzen-ji
timeline.price: free grounds; Sanmon gate ¥600 pp, Hōjō garden ¥600 pp
timeline.note: the Meiji brick aqueduct (Suirokaku) running through a Zen temple is free and the best thing here; the Sanmon climb is the day's optional extra

timeline.what: Walk · Nanzen-ji → Philosopher's Path · 1.0 km · 15 min
Philosopher's Path along the canal
timeline.note: about 2 km one way — turn back at Hōnen-in rather than walking it out to Ginkaku-ji, or the evening becomes a march

timeline.what: Walk · Philosopher's Path → Eikan-dō · 0.9 km · 13 min

brief.Visa & entry: UK passport = visa-free for up to 90 days as a tourist; no ETA scheme applies in 2026. Register both of you on Visit Japan Web for the immigration and customs QR codes. You will be asked for an onward ticket at the desk — have the KIX→LHR booking on your phone. ⚠️ verify at gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/japan before you book, not after.
brief.Holidays & crowds: One collision in the window: Monday 23 Nov, Labour Thanksgiving Day (勤労感謝の日), from date.nager.at. Temples and gardens stay open; the Tsukiji Outer Market and small shops may not, day-trip towns and shinkansen seats fill with domestic travellers, and hotel rates on the 22nd–23rd sit above the rest of the week. Culture Day (3 Nov) is before the window. No festival closures found for these dates in Tokyo, Hakone or Kyoto.
brief.Weather: Same dates last year (Open-Meteo archive, 2025-11-20→29): Tokyo 16 / 7 °C, Hakone 16 / 8 °C, Kyoto 15 / 5 °C; 1–2 wet days in ten, 7–13 mm total. Roughly 10 h of daylight — sunrise ~06:20, sunset ~16:30 in Tokyo and ~16:47 in Kyoto. Kyoto's basin is genuinely cold after dark: the two night illuminations are 2 h standing still at 6 °C. Pack a real coat, not a fleece.
brief.Foliage: Kyoto's 2026 koyo forecast is roughly 25 Nov – 7 Dec with maximum density around 29 Nov – 3 Dec; the Kyoto half of this trip (25–28 Nov) sits on the opening shoulder of that peak. Tokyo runs about a week behind Kyoto for maples but its ginkgos (Yoyogi, Omotesandō) are gold in exactly this week. ⚠️ a forecast, not a fact — an early cold snap moves it a week either way.
brief.Money: Cards work almost everywhere in Tokyo and Kyoto now, but carry ¥15,000–20,000 cash between you: shrine offering boxes, temple entry windows, city buses, Nishiki stalls and the Hakone black-egg hut are cash or IC only. 7-Eleven and Japan Post ATMs take UK cards; most bank ATMs do not. Tipping is not a thing — don't.
brief.Connectivity: eSIM, 10 GB / 8 days, £8–12 each; activate before you leave. Free wifi is widespread and slow. Get IC cards (Suica/Pasmo/ICOCA, or Suica in Apple Wallet) on arrival — they pay for every train, metro, bus and half the vending machines on this route, and ⚠️ physical-card availability for visitors has been on and off since 2023, so the phone wallet is the reliable route.
brief.Plugs: Type A, two flat pins, 100 V. UK plugs do not fit; phone and laptop chargers are dual-voltage so an adapter is enough, but a hairdryer or shaver may not be.
brief.Insurance: Travel-medical cover with repatriation, for both of you. There is no reciprocal healthcare agreement between the UK and Japan and a GHIC is worthless here — a hospital admission is billed in full.
brief.Safety: Low-crime by any standard, and this route needs no dark walks: Shinjuku, Shijō-Karasuma and Hakone-Yumoto are all lit and busy at the hours we use them. The real hazards are physical, not criminal: crowd density at Kiyomizu and Tōfuku-ji in peak week, and wet polished stone on the Sannenzaka steps and the Kiyomizu approach. Bring shoes with grip. Earthquake drill: get under something, stay away from the windows, then follow the staff.
